newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer but faces some resistance.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer but faces some resistance.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer following a late-morning surge which triggered buy stops, enabling the market to run up over 90.00 cents for the most active contract, but little fundamental news lay behind the rally, traders and analysts said.
Fred Demler of E D and F Man said speculative stops were triggered, helped by consumer and hedge buying. A buoyant LME base metals complex also helped New York make gains.

"It's running into a little bit of pressure around the current highs, but my guess is there should be some more stops right around 91.00 cents which could trigger a move right back up to 96.00 cents," Demler said.
December COMEX went out 1.75 cents firmer at 89.65 cents per pound, traded 90.50 to 87.70 cents. Spot September ended 2.00 cents higher at 90.80 cents.
Volume was estimated at 12,000 lots compared to Tuesday's official 8,884 lots.
Floor sources said the December contract faced resistance above 90.00 cents per pound.
Thursday's U.S. housing starts for August - construction is a key copper consuming sector - will be watched by the market. The data is due at 0830 EDT.
